tagline: Sivankoil — Thousand-Year-Old Chola Granite Architecture of Thiruvallur

overview.short: Sivankoil (Raja Raja Choleshwar Mahadevar Temple) is an ancient 11th-century granite Shiva temple in Thiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu. Built under Emperor Raja Raja Chola I, it is celebrated for its classical Dravidian stone carvings and ancient epigraphs.
overview.description: Sivankoil, formally known as the Raja Raja Choleshwar Mahadevar Temple, is an ancient granite Shiva temple located in Thiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu. Commissioned during the reign of the illustrious Emperor Raja Raja Chola I in the early 11th century, the temple exemplifies classical Chola Dravidian architecture with finely carved granite bas-reliefs, a square sanctum vimana, ancient Tamil epigraphical inscriptions recording royal land endowments, and a tranquil rural temple setting.

topPlaces.name: Thiruvallur Veeraraghava Swamy Temple
topPlaces.description: One of the 108 Divya Desams, this grand Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Veeraraghava features a colossal nine-tiered Rajagopuram and the massive Hrittapanasani Pushkarini tank.

image.alt: Colossal Dravidian temple tower at Thiruvallur

topPlaces.name: Thiruvalangadu Vadaranyeswarar Temple
topPlaces.description: One of the five premier cosmic dance halls of Lord Shiva (Rathina Sabhai), where Nataraja performed the Oordhava Thandavam against Goddess Kali. Revered in the Thevaram hymns.

image.alt: Ancient Dravidian stone gopuram and courtyard at Thiruvalangadu

topPlaces.name: Jalandeeswarar Temple, Thakkolam
topPlaces.description: An ancient Paadal Petra Sthalam dating back to the Pallava and Chola eras, situated on the banks of the Kusasthalai River. Famous for its exquisite Dakshinamurthy shrine and historic inscriptions.

image.alt: Granite carvings and pillars of Jalandeeswarar Temple in Thakkolam

topPlaces.name: Othandeeswarar Temple
topPlaces.description: An ancient Chola-period Shiva temple at Thirumazhisai featuring intact granite inscriptions, ornate dvarapalaka statues, and a tranquil village theertham tank.

image.alt: Stone sanctum and gopuram of Othandeeswarar Temple

topPlaces.name: Cooum River Headwaters & Rural Wetlands
topPlaces.description: The pristine rural origin of the Cooum River near Kesavaram features expansive fresh wetlands, ancient water sluices, and agricultural greenery supporting regional water birds.

image.alt: Peaceful freshwater riverbanks and rural groves in Thiruvallur

topPlaces.name: Perambakkam Historic Village
topPlaces.description: Perambakkam is a historic settlement renowned for its role in the 1780 Battle of Pollilur during the Anglo-Mysore War. Today it offers peaceful rural walks and traditional village temples.

image.alt: Traditional village stone shrine and courtyard at Perambakkam

topPlaces.name: Narasingapuram Lakshmi Narasimhar Temple
topPlaces.description: Dedicated to Sri Kalyana Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, this ancient temple features a serene laughing-faced posture of the deity, believed to bring harmony and marital blessings to devotees.

image.alt: Pillared Dravidian entrance and sculpted vimana in Narasingapuram

topPlaces.name: Poondi Reservoir & Satyamoorthy Sagar
topPlaces.description: Poondi Reservoir is an expansive freshwater masonry dam built across the Kosasthalaiyar River, surrounded by peaceful nature trails and scenic viewpoints across vast shimmering blue waters.

image.alt: Expansive water reservoir and stone embankment in Thiruvallur

items.note: Narasingapuram (Tamil: [naɾasoŋɡabɯɾam]) is a village that belongs to the Kadambathur block of Tiruvallur district, located about 55 km from Chennai and 21 km from Arakkonam.

Sri Lakshmi Narasimhar Temple (Tamil: ஸ்ரீ லக்ஷ்மி நரசிம்ஹர் பெருமாள்) is located about 55 km from Chennai and 21 km from Arakkonam, in Narasingapuram, Thiruvallur. The temple is dedicated to Hindu deity Narasimha, who is avatar of Vishnu and his consort Lakshmi.

Deivanayaka Easwarar Temple (தெய்வநாயக ஈஸ்வரர் கோயில்) or Arambeshwarar Temple is a Hindu temple located at Elumiyankottur near Perambakkam village in the Tiruvallur district of Tamil Nadu, India. The presiding deity is Shiva.
Tiruvirkolam (also Thiruvirkolam or Koovam or Coovum or Cooum) is an ancient temple town on the banks of the Koovam River in Tamil Nadu, India. It is located about 70 km from Chennai.
Tripuranthaka Swamy Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Tiruvallur district of Tamil Nadu, India. The presiding deity is Shiva.
Perambakkam is a suburb of Chennai in Tiruvallur district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is a census town in Tiruvallur taluk.

Jalanatheeswarar Temple (also called Thiruvooral) is a Hindu temple dedicated to the deity Shiva and located in Thakkolam, a village in Vellore district in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Shiva is worshipped as Jalanatheeswarar and is represented by the lingam.
Senji is a village in western outskirts of Chennai, located in Tiruvallur district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
